implementation_notes: A `struct` with named fields plus struct-literal initialization is Rust's parameter object: fields may be written in any order, `..Default::default()` fills the optional ones, and clippy's `too_many_arguments` lint actively pushes long argument lists toward it. Derive `Debug`/`Clone`/`PartialEq` (and `Default` when callers should be able to omit fields) to get the value semantics the classic class would hand-write; take `&DrawParams` when the caller keeps ownership, and use the separate builder pattern only when many optional fields are assembled in stages.
pitfalls: `..Default::default()` silently produces wrong values for members that should have been required (an empty `String`, an enum's first variant).
Moving a field out of a borrowed carrier is a partial-move error; borrow or clone explicitly.
Value semantics require derives: without `PartialEq`/`Debug` the carrier has no comparison or printing, unlike a record in other languages.
